source.title: On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy
source.authors: Jing-Yi Cui; Qi Zhang; Yi-Fei Wang; Yi-Sen Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates explanations of SAE latent dimensions by simulating activations and comparing them with actual activations, a different measure from the neuron-explanation claims.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs, compare that share across models or scales, study the classic InceptionV1 examples, or build attribution graphs. Its results on SAE latent auto-interpretability scores bear on the explanation-prediction versions. Synthetic feature-recovery and monosemanticity results, and vision semantic-consistency results, do not measure the shares or outcomes named in V1–V5.
record.test_reason: The study uses an automated simulation-based interpretability score only to compare its own reweighted SAE (WSAE) with a standard SAE. The scored units are SAE latents, not the model's own neurons, and only per-condition average scores are reported, not the share of units explained well. Its results therefore bear on no version. V6 and V7 concern explanations of the model's own neurons and how many of them score well; V1–V5 concern neuron-pole audits, scale, InceptionV1 examples, tools and architecture, and neuron attribution graphs, none of which are studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors prove that standard SAEs generally fail to fully recover ground-truth monosemantic features (feature shrinking and vanishing) except under extreme sparsity, so SAEs should be treated as approximation tools. They propose a reweighted SAE that improves monosemanticity and auto-interpretability scores on synthetic, language (Pythia-160M, Llama-3-8B) and vision (ResNet-18) settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates SAE latent explanations using an auto-interpretability protocol; it does not reproduce the Qwen neuron-pole audit or test the claim's neuron-level job counts.
record.method_sensitivity: Scores vary by layer, SAE objective, weighting parameter α, and the alternative grouped Top-k realization.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard SAE latents on Pythia-160M get average simulation-based auto-interp scores of 71.6–79.5% across layers 0–11 (56.3–69.0% with grouped Top-k). Llama-3-8B SAE latents score 61.4–67.0%. Reweighting raises these by about 0–13 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average simulation-based explanation scores of SAE latents (not neurons) in small and mid-size LMs, and how SAE training objectives shift them.

fits_no_version.finding: Theory and synthetic experiments show standard SAEs fail to fully recover ground-truth monosemantic features (shrinking and vanishing) unless features are extremely sparse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-based dictionaries are approximate rather than faithful recoveries of underlying features, a point bearing on trained-replacement approaches contrasted with neuron-based analysis.

record.problems: The auto-interpretability protocol uses a small evaluation set per feature (5 highly activating and 5 randomly selected fragments for simulation); scores are aggregated, no uncertainty is reported, and the paper's descriptions differ between prediction accuracy and correlation. The study evaluates SAE latents, not the model's own neurons, and does not report a thresholded share of explanations with good scores.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results omitted. Synthetic SAE recovery measures and vision semantic-consistency results are not rows for V6 or V7 because they do not measure prediction of activations from text explanations; the latter are retained as adjacent results only in r51–r53.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-share estimate.
No neuron job shares across models, MoE or scale.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No share of interpretable neurons across tools or architectures. The SAE theory concerns feature recovery by SAEs, not neuron interpretability shares.
No attribution graphs or neuron-based circuits.
No comparison of explanation fit on activating examples vs prediction elsewhere for model neurons.
No simulation scoring of model neurons and no share of neurons with good scores; only average scores for SAE latents.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's description of the auto-interp protocol is internally inconsistent. The main text says prediction accuracy with a Llama3.1-8B summariser; Appendix C.4 says GPT-4 explanations, GPT-3.5 simulation and correlation scoring. Table 3's layer-16 gain is misprinted. Evaluation uses 5 top and 5 random fragments per latent, with no uncertainty reported. The reader's V6 'supports' and V7 'limits_scope' labels are dropped: scores below 100% for SAE latents say nothing about model neurons or the share well explained.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or estimate of the share with one job, two jobs, or unknown jobs.
No measurement of neuron-pole job shares across language models, architectures, or scales.
No study of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
No estimate of interpretable-neuron shares across architectures or tools, nor the stated InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution-graph reconstruction or test of whether model neurons suffice as circuit units.

Tests simulated predictions for SAE latent explanations, not a comparison of explanations that fit activating examples against their prediction on a separately defined set of new examples for individual neurons.

Scores SAE latent explanations with an automated simulation protocol, but does not report the proportion of neurons above a stated good-score threshold; the tested subjects are SAE latents rather than the model's own neurons.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Pythia-160M and Llama-3-8B SAE latent explanations evaluated with automated simulation
reader_labels.reason: The study reports auto-interpretability scores below 100% for the listed conditions, indicating that simulated activations do not perfectly match actual activations; see r1–r50. The score is aggregate and is not reported separately for activating versus other examples.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pythia-160M and Llama-3-8B SAE latent explanations evaluated with automated simulation
reader_labels.reason: The study reports aggregate scores, not the share of neurons meeting a stated good-score threshold, and evaluates SAE latents rather than neurons; see r1–r50.
